claims.text: The material under study is solidified, Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Dynamic behavior in solidified FeNiCrMn is governed by a thermally activated deformation mechanism.
The strain-rate sensitivity of FeNiCrMn is controlled by competition between dislocation glide and grain-boundary-mediated processes.
The temperature dependence of flow stress is controlled by competition between dislocation glide and grain-boundary-mediated processes.
Grain boundaries and dislocation networks are the relevant structural mediators of the dynamic response.
Flow stress in solidified FeNiCrMn will exhibit a strong temperature dependence.
Strain-rate sensitivity in solidified FeNiCrMn will exhibit a strong temperature dependence.
Dislocation glide will dominate deformation at lower temperatures.
Grain-boundary-mediated deformation will dominate at higher temperatures.
The proposed hypothesis applies from -200°C to 800°C.
The proposed hypothesis applies over strain rates from 10^-4 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1.
The hypothesis can be tested by systematically varying temperature and strain rate under tension or compression while measuring flow stress, strain-rate sensitivity, and microstructure.
An absence of strong temperature dependence in both flow stress and strain-rate sensitivity would falsify the hypothesis.
Evidence that other deformation mechanisms dominate would falsify the hypothesis.
